summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Amex to shrink workforce
articles.description: The card company plans to cut 4.5% of its employees to become more “agile and efficient” as it adjusts to more use of artificial intelligence, CEO Stephen Squeri said.

articles.title: Sezzle seeks OCC bank charter
articles.description: The buy now, pay later provider wants a U.S. charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency amid new state rules.

articles.title: Shopping is Muse’s top task: Meta
articles.description: About a quarter of the personal agent’s earliest adopters look to shop, with an average purchase size around $200, Meta’s CEO said.

articles.title: Treasury tallies $270M in suspicious financial aid transactions
articles.description: The department flagged the potentially fraudulent activity as it seeks to stop criminals from stealing student financial aid payments.

articles.title: Paze sets big targets after revamp
articles.description: The wallet’s bank owners are battling Apple and PayPal with an extensive marketing push, touting it as a more secure payment method.

articles.title: Cross River to acquire Accrue
articles.description: Adding the payment and reward services provider would let the bank offer its clients an expanded embedded finance offering. “Payments and loyalty are becoming one,” Cross River’s CEO says.

articles.title: Visa changes fees in Canada
articles.description: A Canadian trade group has urged card networks to reduce their interchange fees and pass those cost savings on to sellers.

articles.title: Fiserv taps AI for retail rethink
articles.description: Merchants are grappling with how their payments technology will handle artificial intelligence-fueled digital commerce, a Fiserv executive said.
